newsitem.title: FRANCE: Expelled Malians turn on French police, plane.
newsitem.headline: Expelled Malians turn on French police, plane.

text.p: A group of Malians expelled from France as illegal immigrants clashed with their French police escort on arrival in Bamako and caused extensive damage to the charter plane which had flown them home, the French interior ministry said on Friday.
Police sources said more than a dozen policemen were injured, two of them seriously.
The ministry said in a statement that 77 Malians, including 28 ex-convicts released from prison, were on board the plane which flew to Bamako on Thursday.
On arrival, several of them attacked some 40 police officers who had escorted them, and the plane, with projectiles they picked up near the runway, police sources said.
"Several police escorting them and were injured and significant damage was caused to the plane. Malian police intervened and the authors of the violence were detained," the statement said.
Police sources said one policeman was injured in the eye and another in the shoulder. A dozen others were less seriously hurt. The cabin was partially ransacked.

In a separate expulsion, 24 Zairean nationals, including seven sent in from Germany, were expelled from France on a charter plane which flew to Kinshasa on Thursday. The ministry said this went off smoothly.
Several human rights and anti-racism groups had protested at the new wave of expulsions.

The MRAP anti-racism organisation called it a "deplorable kick in the teeth" for the thousands who have demonstrated over the past few weeks against a controversial bill cracking down on illegal immigration, approved by the National Assembly late on Thursday,
The centre-right government has now organised 37 such charters since taking office in May 1995 pledging to crack down on illegal immigrants.
